_comment: The HELD-OUT test. Chapters 8-10 of the same film (32:56..46:57), which no knob was fitted on. Nothing is rendered here: the plan is scored against the edit read off this segment, and the cameras all point at the segment itself because only its soundtrack is needed.
_why: A grammar swept against one segment is fitted to it. This is the second segment, and the number it produces is the one worth quoting.
_angles: cam1 is the young host's close-up, cam3 the bearded host's, camW the room -- the shoot has two wide cameras (a studio wide from behind the rig and a frontal two-shot) which the editor uses interchangeably, so the scoring reference merges them. See yt2-fpv33-val.shots-merged.json.

speakers.who: the young host in the grey sweater -- cam1 is his close-up

the bearded host against the purple wall -- cam3 is his close-up. The moment is one where the minority voice is the only one talking; that this voice is his is not read off the edit but off the show: he is the minority speaker in both segments (15.3% and 17.5% of windows), and in the fitted segment that binding produced 77.1% agreement on his own shots.

_hint_trap: The first hint here was placed inside a long close-up of the young host and resolved to the WRONG voice, because this channel cuts to LISTENING faces: being on someone's close-up does not mean he is talking. On a speaker-following channel picking a hint off a close-up is safe; here it is not.
